slides.title:
AI tools for developers
that save real time
slides.subtitle: A clean notebook-style recap of practical tools for coding, shipping, and debugging faster.
slides.side_note:
Beginner-friendly picks
with low setup friction
slides.hero_text: A lightweight map of the best AI-assisted workflows for devs — from IDE help to testing, docs, and issue triage.
slides.takeaway_text: The best tools feel like a calm second brain, not another noisy dashboard.

slides.title:
Use AI inside
your editor first
slides.subtitle: Start where you already write code so the tool fits naturally into your day.

items.title: Autocomplete that understands the file
items.body: Helpful for boilerplate, refactors, and small fixes without leaving your editor.

items.title: Chat over the current project
items.body: Great for asking about architecture, dependencies, and hidden side effects.

items.title: Generate test cases on demand
items.body: Turn edge cases into unit tests before bugs make it to production.

slides.title:
Let AI explain
what broke
slides.subtitle: When something fails, use the model as a patient pair debugger instead of guessing.

items.title: Summarize stack traces
items.body: Ask for a plain-English explanation of the likely root cause and next step.

items.title: Compare similar failures
items.body: Feed multiple logs to spot patterns across environments or releases.

items.title: Draft a fix checklist
items.body: Convert an error report into a short action list for you or your team.

items.title: Write reproduction steps
items.body: Useful when you need to hand the issue to someone else.

slides.title:
Automate the
repeatable parts
slides.subtitle: The biggest gains usually come from removing small, repetitive tasks.

items.title: Release note drafts
items.body: Summarize merged changes into a clear, publish-ready update.

items.title: Docs from code changes
items.body: Keep README files and internal docs closer to the current implementation.

items.title: PR review assistants
items.body: Catch missing tests, inconsistent naming, and risky patterns early.

slides.title:
Use AI as a
collaboration layer
slides.subtitle: The most useful setups help the whole team move with less friction.

items.title: Shared prompt snippets
items.body: Create a common format for tickets, reviews, and incident follow-ups.

items.title: Decision summaries
items.body: Turn long discussions into short, readable action records.

items.title: Onboarding helpers
items.body: Give new teammates a faster path to understanding the codebase.

slides.title:
Build a small AI stack
that your team actually uses
slides.subtitle: Pick one tool, make it part of one workflow, and keep the setup simple.
slides.cta_title: Start with one repeatable pain point
slides.cta_body: Choose a task you do every week — debugging, testing, docs, or reviews — and automate only that first.
